mainTopic: Lashes and sin offerings for forbidden fat and blood, the sources for כרת and לאוין on blood, and lashes for eating מעשר outside ירושלים
overview: The amud opens by asking which תנא a ברייתא follows when it makes someone owe two חטאות for eating forbidden fat. Neither רבי ישמעאל nor רבי יהודה works, because both agree that only one חטאת is brought. So ריש לקיש explains that the person ate from two separate dishes, following רבי יהושע. The גמרא then turns to the lashes for eating חלב of מוקדשין: the רבנן say two sets of lashes and רבי יהודה says three. Their argument depends on whether the verse 'חלב שור' also covers קדשים, and on whether a לאו can be learned from a nearby verse of כרת. Next, the גמרא explains how each side uses the היקש between חלב and blood. For רבי יהודה, it gives blood three sets of lashes. For the רבנן, it teaches when blood joins with flesh to make a full amount, which also covers a snake. רבא then explains the Torah's three mentions of כרת and five לאוין about blood. Finally, רבי אילא rules that eating מעשר of grain, wine and oil outside ירושלים brings three sets of lashes, and the גמרא starts working out which verse is extra; that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא was not explained like רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא was not explained like רבי ישמעאל, because רבי חנינא said רבי ישמעאל agrees that only one חטאת is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that the earlier explanation did not set the ברייתא like רבי ישמעאל. That is because רבי חנינא said: for קרבנות, even רבי ישמעאל agrees a person brings only one חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the earlier explanation avoided רבי ישמעאל. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל may give several sets of lashes for one act of eating. But רבי חנינא says that for a קרבן he agrees only one חטאת is owed. So he cannot be the source of a ברייתא that requires two חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently / we see from here
He established it (explained the ברייתא as following a certain view)
Agrees / concedes
With regard to bringing an offering
Sin offering brought for an accidental sin

steps.confusionAlert: Lashes (מלקות) and sin offerings (חטאות) are counted separately. Someone can get several sets of lashes yet still owe only one חטאת.

phrases.english: Evidently, he did not establish it according to Rabbi Yishmael,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the אמורא earlier on the daf who explained whose view the ברייתא follows.

phrases.english: because Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה הָיָה רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לְעִנְיַן קׇרְבָּן
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael would concede with regard to an offering
that he is liable to only one sin offering,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the earlier explanation of the ברייתא, which comes before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי חנינא, רבי ישמעאל agrees that only one חטאת is brought, so the ברייתא cannot follow him.

steps.title: The same problem applies to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The same reasoning should also rule out רבי יהודה, since רבי אליעזר said רבי יהודה agrees only one חטאת is brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: But now the ברייתא can't be set like רבי יהודה either! רבי אליעזר said: for קרבנות, רבי יהודה agrees that a person brings only one חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same argument against רבי יהודה, the view the ברייתא was actually given to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה gives extra lashes for חלב of מוקדשין. But רבי אליעזר reports that he too agrees only one חטאת is owed. So the reason that pushed out רבי ישמעאל pushes out רבי יהודה as well, and the ברייתא is left without a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Now too / by the same reasoning
It cannot be explained (as following that view)
Brings (an offering)

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא מִתּוֹקְמָא,
phrases.english: Now too, it cannot be established according to Rabbi Yehuda,
for Rabbi Eliezer said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְעִנְיַן קׇרְבָּן
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda would concede with regard to an offering
that one brings only one sin offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא מִתּוֹקְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 1 to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא of two חטאות follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה, like רבי ישמעאל, agrees that only one חטאת is brought, so he cannot be the source of a ruling requiring two.

steps.title: The case is eating from two separate dishes
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting בר תאוטני, says the ברייתא speaks of someone who ate from two dishes, following רבי יהושע, who holds that dishes divide the sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, ריש לקיש said in the name of בר תאוטני: Here we are talking about someone who ate the fat from two separate dishes. This follows רבי יהושע, who says separate dishes make separate sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation. The two חטאות come from eating out of two different dishes, not from the type of fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second חטאת is no longer because the fat falls under two prohibitions. It is because רבי יהושע treats eating from two dishes as two separate acts, even if the person never realized in between that he was sinning. This avoids the problem raised in steps 1 and 2.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower case)
Dishes / bowls
Divide (make each one a separate sin)
According to the view of

steps.whatToRemember: The two חטאות come from two separate dishes, following רבי יהושע, not from two categories of forbidden fat.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר תּאוּטֵנִי:
phrases.english: Rather, Reish Lakish said in the name of bar Ta'utni:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he ate them from two dishes,
and it follows the view of Rabbi Yehoshua,
who says: dishes divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר תּאוּטֵנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 with a new explanation of the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (הכא במאי עסקינן) and placing it with a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two חטאות came from the fat being forbidden under two categories.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two חטאות come from eating out of two separate dishes, following רבי יהושע's rule that dishes divide.

steps.title: Back to the ruling on lashes for forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא itself. Fat of a נבילה brings two sets of lashes, and fat of מוקדשין brings two. רבי יהודה says fat of מוקדשין brings three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the ruling itself. If someone ate the fat of a נבילה, he gets two sets of lashes. If he ate fat of מוקדשין, he gets two sets of lashes. רבי יהודה says: for fat of מוקדשין, he gets three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote the lashes ruling on its own so it can discuss it directly. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fat of a נבילה breaks two prohibitions: חלב and נבילה. Fat of מוקדשין, according to the רבנן, breaks two: חלב and a non-כהן eating holy food. רבי יהודה adds a third set of lashes, and the next step looks at his source.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (returning to a source quoted earlier)
Forbidden fat of an animal
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Animals set aside for the בית המקדש (sacrificial animals)
Receives lashes (מלקות)

phrases.english: The matter itself:
If he ate fat of an animal carcass, he is flogged with two sets of lashes;
fat of sacrificial animals, he is flogged with two sets of lashes;
Rabbi Yehuda says:
fat of sacrificial animals, he is flogged with three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of whose view the ברייתא follows and returns to discuss the lashes ruling itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן give two sets of lashes for חלב of נבילה and two for חלב of מוקדשין. רבי יהודה gives three for חלב of מוקדשין.

steps.title: Three verses fit רבי יהודה, so what is the reasoning of the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי tells רבא that the three verses (two about חלב and one about a זר eating holy food) fit רבי יהודה's three sets of lashes. He asks what the reasoning of the רבנן is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said to רבא: It makes sense for רבי יהודה, because three verses are written: 'a perpetual statute,' 'you shall eat no fat of ox, sheep, or goat,' and 'no outsider shall eat holy food.' That is three prohibitions. But for the רבנן, what is their reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי shows that the verses seem to support רבי יהודה. He then asks how the רבנן can say only two sets of lashes. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two verses about חלב count as two prohibitions for fat of מוקדשין, and the verse about a זר adds a third, giving רבי יהודה's three. The רבנן seem to ignore one of these verses. So רב שיזבי asks what they do with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (sets up a contrast with 'אלא')
Verses
A non-כהן
Negative commandments (prohibitions that bring lashes)
What is their reasoning?

phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi said to Rava:
Granted, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
this is why the verses are written:
"It shall be a perpetual statute"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:17

phrases.aramaic: ״כׇּל חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב וָעֵז לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ״,
phrases.english: "You shall eat no fat of ox, or sheep, or goat"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:23

phrases.english: "And no non-priest shall eat of the holy food"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:10

phrases.english: these are three prohibitions.
But according to the Rabbis, what is their reasoning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the רבנן's ruling in step 4, given the verses that support רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's ruling of only two sets of lashes for חלב of מוקדשין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three verses are written, which match רבי יהודה's three sets of lashes. The רבנן seem to leave one verse unexplained.

steps.title: The רבנן split the two חלב verses between קדשים and חולין
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that the לאו of 'חקת עולם' is about קדשים and the לאו of 'חלב שור' is about חולין. So each piece of חלב falls under only one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They hold: the prohibition of 'a perpetual statute' is about sacrificial animals, and the prohibition of 'fat of ox' is about non-sacred animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב שיזבי's question about the reasoning of the רבנן. They say each חלב verse covers a different kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שיזבי pointed out that there are three verses, so three sets of lashes seemed reasonable. The רבנן answer that the two חלב verses do not both apply to the same piece of fat. One is for קדשים and one is for חולין, so חלב of קדשים gets one חלב lash plus one for a זר eating holy food. That makes two.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah prohibition (a 'do not'), which brings lashes
'A perpetual statute', the verse forbidding חלב in the קרבנות section
'Fat of ox', the verse forbidding the fat of ox, sheep and goat
Sacrificial animals, holy animals
Regular, non-sacred animals

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key to the whole מחלוקת. The number of lashes depends on whether both חלב verses can apply to the same animal.

phrases.english: They hold:
phrases.notes: 'They' means the רבנן, who said only two sets of lashes for חלב of קדשים.

phrases.english: the prohibition of 'a perpetual statute' is about sacrificial animals,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:17

phrases.english: and the prohibition of 'fat of ox' is about non-sacred animals.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 about the reasoning of the רבנן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the verses: each verse is assigned to a different kind of animal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both חלב verses apply to חלב of קדשים, which would give three sets of lashes
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one חלב verse applies to קדשים, so there are only two sets of lashes

steps.title: Why the Torah needed a verse for חולין
steps.stepSummary: Both verses are needed. If the Torah had forbidden חלב only for קדשים, we would think חולין is more lenient, so it wrote 'כל חלב שור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both are needed. If the Torah had written it only about sacrificial animals, I would have said that only sacrificial animals, which are strict, have forbidden fat, but not regular animals. That is why the Torah wrote 'any fat of ox.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that both verses are necessary, so neither one is extra. This step gives the first half: why the חולין verse is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each verse covers a different case, someone might ask why the Torah did not just write one rule for everything. The answer is that we could not learn חולין from קדשים, because קדשים are stricter in general.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They are needed', meaning both verses are necessary and neither is extra
'I would have said', a mistaken first thought
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
'They are strict'

phrases.english: And both are needed,
for if the Merciful One had written it only about sacrificial animals,
I would have said:
it is sacrificial animals that are strict,
so their fat is forbidden,
but regular animals, I would say no,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא: ״כׇּל חֵלֶב שׁוֹר״.
phrases.english: that is why the Merciful One wrote: 'Any fat of ox.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the split in step 6 by showing the חולין verse is necessary
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'כל חלב שור' verse is needed for חולין, because it could not be learned from קדשים, which are stricter

steps.title: Why the Torah needed a verse for קדשים, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written only 'כל חלב שור', we would think קדשים fat is allowed, since קדשים meat becomes allowed. So both verses are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had written only 'any fat of ox', I would have said only regular animals' fat is forbidden, because it is never allowed. But sacrificial animals, which do become allowed, I would think that since their meat became allowed, their fat became allowed too. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the 'both are needed' argument. It shows why the קדשים verse is needed, and then concludes that both verses are necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חולין fat is always forbidden. The meat of a קרבן, though, starts out forbidden and later becomes allowed. Without its own verse, we might have thought its fat becomes allowed along with the meat. So the קדשים verse cannot be learned from the חולין verse either.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Was permitted from its general category', meaning something that started forbidden and became allowed in some way
Consecrated animals, the same as קדשים
'Became permitted'

steps.whatToRemember: According to the רבנן, the two חלב verses do not overlap: 'חקת עולם' is for קדשים and 'חלב שור' is for חולין. Each is needed because neither case can be learned from the other. So חלב of קדשים gets only two sets of lashes.

phrases.english: And if it had written only 'Any fat of ox,'
I would have said:
it is the fat of regular animals that is forbidden
because it was never permitted from its general prohibition,
but the fat of sacrificial animals, which was permitted from its general prohibition,
phrases.notes: A קרבן's meat starts out forbidden to eat, but it becomes allowed after the blood is sprinkled.

phrases.english: I would have said:
since their meat was permitted,
their fat was permitted as well,
so both are needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב: ״כׇּל חֵלֶב שׁוֹר״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'both are needed' argument begun in step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both חלב verses are necessary, each for its own case, which supports the רבנן's count of two sets of lashes

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads 'חלב שור' as also about קדשים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that the 'חלב שור' verse appears in the section about קדשים. So it also applies to קדשים, which gives three sets of lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה holds: when 'fat of ox' is written, it is written in the section about sacrificial animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבי יהודה's view. He holds that the 'חלב שור' verse also applies to קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'חלב שור' verse sits in a section that talks about קרבנות. So רבי יהודה learns it from its context and applies it to קדשים too. That means חלב of קדשים is covered by both חלב verses plus the זר verse, which makes three sets of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In the section about sacrificial animals'
'It is written'
A rule learned from its surrounding context

steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת depends on how to read 'חלב שור'. The רבנן apply it only to חולין, which gives two sets of lashes. רבי יהודה also applies it to קדשים because of where it is written, which gives three.

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה holds:
when 'fat of ox' is written,
it is written in the section about sacrificial animals.
phrases.notes: Right after it, ויקרא 7:25 speaks of an animal brought as an offering to ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: כִּי כְּתִיב ״חֵלֶב שׁוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts רבי יהודה's reading with the רבנן's split in steps 6 through 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of its context, 'חלב שור' also applies to קדשים, so all three verses apply to חלב of קדשים

steps.title: Do the Rabbis reject learning from context?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the רבנן's view means they reject the basic rule of דבר הלמד מעניינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But should we conclude that the רבנן hold we do not learn a matter from its context?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן. If רבי יהודה learns from the surrounding section that 'חלב שור' covers קדשים, then the רבנן seem to reject that whole method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, רבי יהודה applied 'חלב שור' to קדשים because it sits in the קדשים section. That is the rule of דבר הלמד מעניינו. Since the רבנן disagree, it looks like they reject this standard rule, and that would be very hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; can we infer from this
A matter learned from its context, meaning the section a verse appears in
We learn or derive

phrases.english: But can we infer that the Rabbis hold:
we do not learn a matter from its context?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי יהודה's reasoning from Step 9 and asks what it implies about the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רבנן disagree with a derivation from context, they seem to reject דבר הלמד מעניינו, which is an accepted rule

steps.title: Everyone learns from context; the argument is about learning from כרת
steps.stepSummary: Everyone accepts דבר הלמד מעניינו. They argue only about whether a לאו can be learned from a nearby verse of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees we learn a matter from its context. They argue about this: רבי יהודה holds we learn a לאו from another לאו, and also a לאו from כרת. The רבנן hold we learn a לאו from another לאו, but not a לאו from כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both sides accept learning from context. It then shows where they really disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nearby verse that speaks about קדשים is a verse of כרת, not a לאו. רבי יהודה lets that כרת verse shape the meaning of the לאו of 'חלב שור', so the לאו covers קדשים too. The רבנן only let a לאו be learned from another לאו, so for them 'חלב שור' stays limited to חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
They disagree
A negative commandment, punished by lashes
Being cut off, a heavenly punishment

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is not about learning from context. It is about whether a לאו can be learned from a כרת verse.

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees
that a matter is learned from its context,
and they disagree about this:
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
we learn a prohibition from a prohibition
and a prohibition from כרת,
phrases.notes: The verse right next to 'חלב שור' gives כרת for eating חלב of animals brought as offerings.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold:
a prohibition from a prohibition we learn,
a prohibition from כרת we do not learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן reject learning from context
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides learn from context. They argue only about whether a לאו can be learned from כרת

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with 'כל חלב וכל דם'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the לאו for קדשים from 'חלב שור'. So what is the verse 'כל חלב וכל דם לא תאכלו' needed for?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי יהודה, what does the verse 'You shall eat no fat and no blood' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the verse 'כל חלב וכל דם לא תאכלו' is for in רבי יהודה's view. The next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן use this verse (the חקת עולם verse) as the לאו for קדשים. רבי יהודה already gets a לאו for קדשים from 'חלב שור'. So for him, this verse seems to have no job left.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to teach?
Forbidden fats of an animal

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yehuda,
"You shall eat no fat and no blood",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:17

phrases.english: what does it come for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי יהודה gets the קדשים לאו elsewhere, the גמרא checks whether this verse becomes extra
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's use of the verses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse in the Torah should not be left without a purpose

steps.title: The verse compares blood to חלב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses the verse for a היקש: just as חלב brings two sets of lashes, so does blood. The חכמים say blood has only one warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for a comparison, as a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall eat no fat and no blood.' Just as for חלב one gets two sets of lashes, so for blood one gets two sets of lashes. These are the words of רבי יהודה. The חכמים say: blood has only one warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה uses the verse to link blood with חלב. It brings a ברייתא to prove this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because חלב and blood are mentioned together in one verse, רבי יהודה treats them the same. Since חלב gets two sets of lashes, blood does too. The חכמים disagree and give blood only one warning.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison between two things mentioned together in one verse
Receives lashes
A warning, meaning a לאו

steps.whyThisMatters: This היקש is what the next step will question.

phrases.english: He needs it for a comparison,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: ״כׇּל חֵלֶב וְכׇל דָּם לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ״,
phrases.english: as it is taught: "You shall eat no fat and no blood",
just as for fat one is lashed twice,
so too for blood one is lashed twice,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages say:
it has only one warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the verse a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי יהודה the verse has no use
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches a היקש that gives blood two sets of lashes, like חלב

steps.title: Blood already has two verses, so why is a היקש needed?
steps.stepSummary: חלב gets two sets of lashes because two verses forbid it. Blood also has two verses forbidding it, so it should get two sets of lashes without a היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about חלב, that it gets two sets of lashes without a היקש? It is because two verses are written about it: 'You shall eat no fat and no blood' and 'You shall eat no fat of ox or sheep.' Blood should also get two sets of lashes without a היקש, since two לאוין are written about it: 'You shall eat no fat and no blood' and 'You shall eat no blood in any of your dwellings, of bird or of animal'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 13. If blood already has two verses forbidding it, the היקש seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב gets two sets of lashes simply because two verses forbid it. Blood also appears in two separate verses. So the same reasoning should already give blood two sets of lashes, and the היקש would have nothing to add.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Two verses
Negative commandments (plural of לאו)

steps.confusionAlert: The verse 'כל חלב וכל דם' is counted for both חלב and blood. Each one gets a second verse of its own.

phrases.english: And what is different about fat
that one is lashed twice without a comparison,
because two verses are written about it:
"You shall eat no fat and no blood",
"no fat of ox or sheep"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:23

phrases.english: Blood too, without a comparison,
should get lashed twice,
since two prohibitions are written about it:
"You shall eat no fat and no blood",
"And you shall eat no blood
in all your dwellings
of bird or of animal"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:26

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא חֵלֶב דְּלוֹקֶה שְׁתַּיִם בְּלָא הֶיקֵּישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the היקש given in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's היקש between blood and חלב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood has two verses just like חלב, so it should get two sets of lashes without any היקש, which makes the היקש unnecessary

steps.title: Reworking the comparison: three sets of lashes, not two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of רבי יהודה's היקש. It now teaches that blood brings three sets of lashes, just like חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this: just as one is flogged three times for חלב, so too one is flogged three times for blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The question in step 14 knocked out the 'two sets of lashes' reading. So the גמרא gives a new reading of the היקש: חלב brings three sets of lashes, and so does blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 showed that blood already has two verses forbidding it, so a היקש teaching 'two sets' would add nothing. The new reading counts a third לאו, the ban on a זר eating holy food, and says the היקש gives blood that third set of lashes too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא changes how a teaching should be read
Is flogged, receives lashes
Three (sets of lashes)

phrases.english: Rather, say:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is giving up the 'two sets of lashes' reading from step 13 and offering a new one.

phrases.english: just as for fat one is flogged three times,
phrases.notes: Two lashes for the two verses about חלב, and a third for a זר eating holy food (ויקרא 22:10).

phrases.english: so too for blood one is flogged three times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by rereading the היקש as teaching three sets of lashes instead of two.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The היקש taught that blood brings two sets of lashes, like חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The היקש teaches that blood brings three sets of lashes, like חלב, including the לאו of זרות.

steps.title: Blood already has three prohibitions, so why the comparison?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: חלב gets three sets of lashes because of two verses plus the זרות ban. Blood has the same three, so the היקש still seems unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about חלב, that one is flogged three times? It is because two prohibitions are written about it, plus the prohibition of a זר eating holy food. That makes three. Blood has the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading in the same way it attacked the old one. If blood naturally has the same three prohibitions as חלב, the היקש teaches nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 asked this about two lashes. Now the same question is asked about three. Blood also has two verses and is also holy food that a זר may not eat, so it seems to reach three sets of lashes on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Used to ask why one case is treated differently from another
The prohibition against a non-כהן eating holy food (ויקרא 22:10)
So that makes three

phrases.english: And what is different about fat
that one is flogged three times?
Because these two prohibitions are written about it,
and the prohibition of a non-priest –
so that makes three?
Blood too!
phrases.notes: Blood also has two verses plus the זרות ban, so it should get three lashes even without the היקש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the logic of step 14's challenge against the new 'three lashes' reading of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the היקש in its new reading (three sets of lashes).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood already has the same three prohibitions as חלב on its own, so a היקש teaching three sets of lashes adds nothing.

steps.title: The comparison is needed because blood is left out of the impurity ban
steps.stepSummary: The היקש is needed. Blood is left out of the prohibition of eating holy food while impure, so we might have thought it is also left out of the זרות prohibition. The היקש teaches that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since blood is excluded from the law of impurity, let it also be excluded from the law of a non-priest. So the היקש teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 16. Without the היקש, we could have wrongly thought that a זר who eats blood of קדשים is not punished for זרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who eats blood of קדשים while טמא is not liable for eating קדשים בטומאה, so blood is treated as less than full holy food in that area. We might have stretched that and left blood out of the זרות ban too. The היקש to חלב blocks that, so blood keeps all three sets of lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
It might have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
Was excluded, left out of a law
Ritual impurity; here, the ban on eating holy food while impure
It teaches us (something we would not have known)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, eating blood of קדשים brings three sets of lashes. The היקש to חלב is needed so we don't leave blood out of the זרות ban just because it is left out of the טומאה ban.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two bans. Blood is left out of the טומאה ban (eating holy food while impure), but the היקש teaches that it is still included in the זרות ban (a non-כהן eating holy food).

phrases.english: It was needed,
it might have entered your mind to say:
since blood is excluded from impurity –
phrases.notes: Eating blood of קדשים while impure doesn't break the ban on eating holy food in a state of טומאה.

phrases.english: let it be excluded from the ban on a non-priest,
so the juxtaposition teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by showing the היקש prevents a mistaken conclusion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing the source is needed to block a wrong assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since blood is excluded from the טומאה ban, it would also be excluded from the זרות ban, so a זר eating it would get only two sets of lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The היקש to חלב teaches that blood is included in the זרות ban, so it brings three sets of lashes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the defense of רבי יהודה's use of the verse 'כל חלב וכל דם לא תאכלו' and sets up the same question for the רבנן.

steps.title: What is the comparison for according to the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say blood of קדשים has only one warning. If so, they do not use the היקש to add lashes, so the גמרא asks what the היקש teaches in their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the רבנן, what does the היקש come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: After explaining how רבי יהודה uses the היקש, the גמרא turns to the רבנן. It challenges them: if blood gets only one set of lashes, what is the היקש between חלב and דם for? This question sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links חלב and דם, and a היקש should teach something. רבי יהודה uses it for extra lashes, but the רבנן reject extra lashes for blood (step 13). So the גמרא needs to find another purpose for it in their view.

keyTerms.meaning: היקש: a comparison learned from two things placed together in one verse
What does it come for? Asks what a source teaches

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis,
what does the juxtaposition come for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained רבי יהודה's use of the היקש, the גמרא now challenges the רבנן's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the רבנן that blood of קדשים has only one warning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse links חלב and דם in a היקש. If the רבנן don't use it to add lashes for blood, the היקש seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: The היקש teaches which blood joins with the flesh
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, the היקש teaches about joining amounts. Blood of a creature whose blood is separate from its flesh does not join with the flesh, just like חלב. Blood of שרצים does join with their flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן need the היקש for what a ברייתא teaches: 'You shall eat no fat and no blood.' Fat has a special feature: it is separate from the animal's meat, so the two do not join together. Blood is the same when it comes from a creature whose blood is separate from its flesh. I leave out the blood of שרצים. Their blood is not separate from their flesh, so the two do join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 18. Even the רבנן need the היקש of חלב and blood, because it teaches a rule about when blood joins with flesh to make a full amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלב is forbidden, but the meat of a kosher animal is permitted. So eating half a כזית of each does not add up to a forbidden כזית. The היקש teaches that blood works the same way whenever the blood has its own separate status from the flesh. שרצים are the exception: their blood and flesh have the same status, so they add up together.

keyTerms.meaning: They join together to make up the minimum amount needed for liability
Separate from its flesh, meaning it has a different status from the flesh
Creeping creatures, which are forbidden to eat
Special or unique, the feature that the comparison is based on

steps.confusionAlert: 'Separate from its flesh' does not mean the blood is physically apart from the meat. It means the blood has a different law than the flesh, so the two cannot be counted together.

phrases.english: They need it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the היקש of חלב and blood that Step 18 asked about.

phrases.english: "You shall eat no fat and no blood,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:17

phrases.english: just as fat is special
in that its fat is separate from its meat,
phrases.notes: The fat is forbidden, but the meat is permitted.

phrases.english: and they do not join with each other,
so too blood, of a creature whose blood is separate from its flesh.
I will leave out the blood of creeping creatures,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל דְּאֵין דָּמָן חָלוּק מִבְּשָׂרָן – מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.english: since their blood is not separate from their flesh, they do join.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18's question by giving the היקש a different job for the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the היקש a new purpose: rules about joining amounts, not extra lashes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a job for the היקש, the רבנן's reading of the פסוק would seem pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The היקש teaches that blood joins with the flesh only when the blood does not have its own separate status, as with שרצים.

steps.title: The rule for שרצים already comes from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: we already know from 'וזה לכם הטמא' that the blood and flesh of a שרץ join together. So why is this היקש needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we learn this from here? We learn it from there: 'And these are impure to you.' This teaches that the blood of a שרץ and the שרץ itself join with each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 19. The rule that a שרץ's blood joins with its flesh is already taught by a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If another ברייתא already learns from ויקרא 11:29 that a שרץ's blood and flesh join, then the היקש teaches nothing new. That puts us back to Step 18's question: what is the היקש for in the view of the רבנן?

keyTerms.meaning: Is it learned from here?
It is learned from there, a different source
A single creeping creature

phrases.english: But is it learned from here?
It is learned from there:
"And these are impure to you"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:29

phrases.english: teaches about the blood of the creeping creature and the creature itself
that they join with each other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 19's answer by showing the rule already has another source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the היקש is needed to teach that a שרץ's blood joins with its flesh.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another פסוק already teaches this, so the היקש would be extra.

steps.title: The other verse covers טומאה; the היקש covers eating
steps.stepSummary: The other פסוק only teaches that a שרץ's blood and flesh join for טומאה. The היקש is needed to teach that they also join for the prohibition of eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not for the היקש, you might have thought that this rule applies only to impurity, but for eating, you might say they do not join. The היקש teaches us that they join for eating too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in Step 20. It shows that the two sources teach different things, so the היקש is not extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וזה לכם הטמא' talks about impurity, so it only proves that a שרץ's blood and flesh join to make the amount that makes something טמא. Without the היקש, we might think that for the איסור of eating they stay separate. The היקש extends the joining rule to eating.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say (the mistaken first thought)
Ritual impurity
Eating, meaning the prohibition of eating
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, the היקש of חלב and blood is not about extra lashes. It teaches that blood with its own separate status does not join with the flesh. A שרץ's blood does join with its flesh, and this applies to eating, not only to טומאה.

phrases.english: If not for the היקש,
you might have thought to say:
this applies only to impurity,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule from 'וזה לכם הטמא' that a שרץ's blood and flesh join.

phrases.english: but for eating, say it does not,
so the היקש teaches us this for eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו הֶיקֵּישָׁא, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by giving each source its own area: impurity versus eating.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources into separate areas of law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שרץ's blood and flesh join only for טומאה, not for the prohibition of eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The היקש teaches that they join for eating as well.

steps.title: A snake's blood and flesh join together
steps.stepSummary: רבינא draws a practical ruling from the previous step: a snake's blood and flesh add up together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Therefore, the blood of a snake and its flesh join together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a practical ruling based on what we just learned. A snake's blood and its flesh can be added together to reach the amount needed for punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21 we learned that the היקש makes blood and flesh join for the prohibition of eating, when the blood is not separate from the flesh. רבינא applies this to a snake. So eating half a כזית of snake blood with half a כזית of snake flesh counts as a full כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore. It draws a result from what was just said.
Snake
They join together. Two things are added up to reach the required amount.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Therefore,
the blood of a snake and its flesh join together.
phrases.notes: Together they can make up the olive-size amount (כזית) needed to be punished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion of step 21 to a specific creature.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A snake's blood and flesh combine to make up a כזית for the prohibition of eating.

steps.title: Isn't this just the היקש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבינא added, since the היקש already teaches this.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? This is just the היקש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבינא. His ruling seems to add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The היקש already said that any creature whose blood is not separate from its flesh has blood and flesh that join. A snake fits that rule. So why did רבינא need to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? Used when a statement seems to add nothing new.
The היקש. A comparison the Torah makes by placing two things side by side.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
This is just the היקש!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? הַיְינוּ הֶיקֵּישָׁא!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 22 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling that only repeats what an existing source says is unnecessary.

steps.title: A snake might have been treated differently from a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought only a שרץ, which carries טומאה, has blood that joins. רבינא teaches that the rule covers a snake too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: a שרץ, which was included for טומאה, is included for eating. A snake, which was not included for טומאה, is not included for eating. So the היקש teaches us that it means anything whose blood is not separate from its flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבינא needed to speak. We might have limited the rule to the eight impure שרצים, and he teaches that a snake is included too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שרץ's blood joins its flesh for טומאה, so we might have linked eating to that and thought the rule only applies to creatures that carry טומאה. A snake does not carry טומאה, so we might have left it out. רבינא teaches that the היקש depends only on whether the blood is separate from the flesh, not on טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought. It introduces a mistaken assumption.
Was included. Brought in by a source in the Torah.
Separate. Different from something else.

steps.confusionAlert: A snake is not one of the eight שרצים that carry טומאה. Even so, it still falls under the eating rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Blood and flesh join for eating whenever the blood is not separate from the flesh. Whether the creature carries טומאה does not matter.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
a שרץ, whose blood was included for impurity,
is included for eating.
a snake, whose blood was not included for impurity,
is not included for eating.
So the היקש teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִילֵּי דְּאֵין דָּמוֹ חָלוּק מִבְּשָׂרוֹ מַשְׁמַע.
phrases.english: it means anything whose blood is not separate from its flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the statement is needed to block a mistaken assumption (סלקא דעתך).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a שרץ, whose blood joins for טומאה, would have blood that joins for eating. A snake would not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The היקש covers every creature whose blood is not separate from its flesh, including a snake.

steps.title: Three mentions of כרת for blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the Torah's three mentions of כרת for blood cover three kinds of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are three כריתות stated about blood. What are they for? One is for blood of non-sacred animals, one is for blood of קדשים, and one is for דם התמצית.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא says the Torah mentions כרת for eating blood three times, and each mention teaches about a different kind of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah usually does not repeat itself for nothing. So רבא gives each mention its own job: ordinary blood, blood of sacrifices, and the blood that oozes out after the main flow at slaughter. This sets up the challenges that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off. A heavenly punishment for serious sins.
Blood of non-sacred animals
Blood of sacrificial animals
Exudate blood. Blood that oozes out after the first gush at slaughter.

phrases.english: Rava said:
There are three mentions of כרת stated about blood.
What are they for?
One is for the blood of non-sacred animals,
one is for the blood of sacrificial animals,
and one is for exudate blood.
phrases.notes: This is the blood that slowly oozes out after the main gush when the animal is slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שָׁלֹשׁ כָּרֵיתוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about the sources for כרת for blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the three mentions of כרת for blood teaches one kind: חולין, קדשים, and דם התמצית.

steps.title: This only works for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא's third כרת fits רבי יהודה, who holds there is כרת for דם התמצית. It quotes the ברייתא as the setup for a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to רבי יהודה, as it was taught: דם התמצית is under a warning. רבי יהודה says: it carries כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רבא. It shows that his third כרת matches רבי יהודה's view in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the first opinion holds that דם התמצית only carries a plain prohibition, with no כרת. רבי יהודה says it carries כרת. רבא's reading, where one כרת is for דם התמצית, fits only רבי יהודה. That opens the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well. The first half of a challenge, meaning 'this fits one view, but...'
A warning. A plain prohibition without כרת.

phrases.english: This works well according to רבי יהודה,
as it was taught in a ברייתא:
Exudate blood is under a plain prohibition,
רבי יהודה says: it carries כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to רבא's statement by tying it to one side of a dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's third כרת, the one for דם התמצית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reading only fits רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא, which sets up the question about the רבנן.

steps.title: What is the third כרת for according to the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן give no כרת for דם התמצית, so the גמרא asks what the third mention teaches in their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the רבנן, what does that third mention come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. According to the רבנן, the third כרת seems to have no job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that דם התמצית only has a plain prohibition. So the third mention of כרת cannot be for דם התמצית in their view. The גמרא asks what it teaches instead.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come for? A question about what a source is teaching.

phrases.english: But according to the רבנן,
what does that one come to teach?
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the third mention of כרת for blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the הניחא challenge begun in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's three כריתות according to the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רבנן give no כרת for דם התמצית, the third mention has no purpose in their view.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה learns this כרת from 'כל דם'
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יהודה does not need the third כרת for דם התמצית, because he learns it from the words 'כל דם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי יהודה, he learns the כרת from the words 'כל דם'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge. Even for רבי יהודה, רבא's reading does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learns כרת for דם התמצית from the extra words 'כל דם', meaning 'any blood'. So he does not need the third mention of כרת for it. Now the third mention seems to have no job according to either view.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it from. He derives the law from a certain source.
Any blood. The words in the פסוק that include every kind of blood.

steps.whyThisMatters: This leaves רבא's statement under challenge from both sides. The גמרא will need to explain the third כרת in a new way.

phrases.english: And even according to רבי יהודה,
he learns the כרת from 'any blood'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:10

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, כָּרֵת נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִן ״כׇּל דָּם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge from step 27 by showing it applies even to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that one כרת is for דם התמצית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה already has another source ('כל דם') for כרת on דם התמצית, so the third mention is still unexplained.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי יהודה learns from 'כל דם'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves that רבי יהודה learns כרת for דם חולין and דם התמצית from the extra word 'כל' in 'כל דם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says: The verse could have said just 'blood'. Why does it say 'any blood'? From 'blood' alone I would only know about blood of קדשים, the blood the animal's life leaves with. How do I know about blood of חולין and דם התמצית? The verse says 'any blood'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the claim it just made, that רבי יהודה gets כרת for דם התמצית from 'כל דם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the extra word 'כל' as widening the law. Without it, the verse would cover only sacrificial blood, the blood that brings כפרה. With 'כל', it also covers חולין blood and דם התמצית. So רבא's third כרת is not needed even for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse comes to teach us; it points to an extra word in the פסוק
Blood of animals brought as sacrifices
Blood the animal's life leaves with, the main blood of slaughter
Blood of ordinary animals that are not sacrifices

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:10

phrases.english: The verse could have said 'blood'; why does it say 'any blood'?
I would only have the blood of sacrificial animals
the blood the animal's life leaves with,
From where do I know about blood of ordinary animals and blood that oozes out?
The verse says: 'Any blood'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the challenge in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not need the third כרת for דם התמצית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה learns דם חולין and דם התמצית from 'כל דם'.

steps.title: Rereading רבא's three כרתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes how we read רבא: the three כרתות are for דם חולין, דם קדשים, and דם כיסוי, not for דם התמצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this is what רבא means: one mention is for blood of חולין, one for blood of קדשים, and one for דם כיסוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying רבא's third כרת was not about דם התמצית at all; it was about דם כיסוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that neither the רבנן nor רבי יהודה needed a third כרת for דם התמצית. So the third כרת is moved to דם כיסוי, the blood of a wild animal or bird. Now רבא's teaching works for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא changes how a statement is read
Blood that must be covered: the blood of a wild animal or a bird
Being cut off, a heavy punishment from Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean דם התמצית is permitted. The גמרא is only saying that רבא's three כרתות do not include it.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
one is for blood of ordinary animals,
and one is for blood of sacrificial animals,
and one is for the blood that must be covered.
phrases.notes: That is the blood of a wild animal or bird, which has a מצוה of covering (ויקרא 17:13).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 27-29 by rereading רבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's third כרת was for דם התמצית, which does not work for either the רבנן or רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא's third כרת is for דם כיסוי, which works for everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: The three כרתות for blood are: דם חולין, דם קדשים, and דם כיסוי.

steps.title: רבא explains the five לאוין about blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the Torah's five לאוין about blood cover five kinds: חולין, קדשים, כיסוי, איברין, and תמצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Why are there five לאוין said about blood? One for blood of חולין, one for blood of קדשים, one for דם כיסוי, one for blood in the limbs, and one for דם התמצית.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new teaching: each of the five לאוין about blood stands for a different kind of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are more לאוין than כרתות. דם איברין and דם התמצית each get their own לאו, even though they were not part of the three כרתות. So these bloods are forbidden by a לאו even where there is no כרת for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Negative commandments, 'do not' prohibitions in the Torah
Blood that stays inside the animal's limbs
Blood that oozes out slowly after the main flow of slaughter

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that דם התמצית is still clearly forbidden by a לאו, even for the רבנן who give no כרת for it.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Why are there five prohibitions stated about blood?

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת לְדַם חוּלִּין, וְאַחַת לְדַם קָדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: One is for blood of ordinary animals, and one for blood of sacrificial animals,
and one for the blood that must be covered,
and one for the blood in the limbs,
and one for blood that oozes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: חֲמִשָּׁה לָאוִין הָאֲמוּרִין בְּדָם לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After fixing the three כרתות, a second teaching of רבא explains the five לאוין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five לאוין about blood cover דם חולין, דם קדשים, דם כיסוי, דם איברין, and דם התמצית.

steps.title: Three sets of lashes for eating tithe of grain, wine and oil
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא rules that one who eats מעשר of grain, wine and oil outside ירושלים is lashed three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא said: If someone ate tithe of grain, wine and oil (outside ירושלים), he gets three sets of lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אילא. Eating מעשר שני of grain, wine and oil outside ירושלים gets three separate sets of מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is one פסוק that forbids eating all three kinds outside ירושלים. Even so, רבי אילא counts each kind as its own sin, with its own lashes. The next step challenges this.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe of grain. Here it means מעשר שני, which must be eaten in ירושלים.
Wine (new wine).
Olive oil.
He is lashed, meaning he gets מלקות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Illa says:
If one ate the tithe of grain, wine, and oil
phrases.notes: He means eating it outside ירושלים, which is where this tithe must be eaten. See דברים 12:17.

phrases.english: he is lashed three times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: רבי אילא's ruling about eating מעשר outside ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating מעשר of grain, wine and oil outside ירושלים gives three separate sets of מלקות.

steps.title: One is not lashed for a general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this is a לאו שבכללות, and no lashes are given for that.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we have a rule that one is not lashed for a general prohibition that covers several things!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אילא. One לאו that lumps several things together does not give lashes at all, let alone three sets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition against eating מעשר outside ירושלים is one לאו that names grain, wine and oil together. A לאו like that is called a לאו שבכללות, and the rule is that it gives no מלקות. So how can רבי אילא give three sets of lashes?

keyTerms.meaning: A general prohibition: one לאו that covers several different things at once.
We do not give lashes.

phrases.english: But one is not lashed
for a general prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֵין לוֹקִין עַל לָאו שֶׁבִּכְלָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אילא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילא's ruling of three sets of lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is a single לאו covering three items, and such a לאו gives no lashes, so three sets of lashes should not be possible.

steps.title: The verses are extra
steps.stepSummary: Answer: this case is different, because the פסוקים are extra and come to teach something.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because the verses are extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the usual rule does not apply here, because one of the פסוקים is extra. The next step will show exactly how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a לאו שבכללות gives no lashes. But if a פסוק is not needed for its simple meaning, it can be used to teach that each item is its own separate לאו. Then each one gives its own lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different.
The verses are extra (not needed for their plain meaning).

phrases.english: It is different here,
because the verses are extra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception to the general rule, based on an extra פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single לאו that lists three items should give no lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the פסוק is extra, it comes to split the לאו into separate prohibitions, each with lashes.

steps.title: Showing which verse is extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the first פסוק already forbids eating outside, so the second פסוק is extra and comes to split the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah already wrote: 'And you shall eat before ה׳ your God the tithe of your grain, your wine and your oil.' That teaches: inside (ירושלים) yes, outside no. So why did the Torah need to write: 'You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain, your wine and your oil'? To split them into separate prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that a פסוק is extra. It shows that the ban on eating outside ירושלים is already known from another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'eat before ה׳' already tells us that eating is allowed only inside ירושלים, so eating outside is forbidden. That makes the פסוק 'you may not eat within your gates' seem unneeded. So it is used to teach לחלק: each of grain, wine and oil is its own לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (the Torah already wrote…). It opens an argument that something is extra.
Inside, meaning in ירושלים.
Outside ירושלים.
In your gates, meaning in your own towns outside ירושלים.
To split: to make each item its own separate prohibition.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic way out of the rule of לאו שבכללות. When a פסוק is extra, it can split one general לאו into several לאוין that each carry lashes.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One wrote:
"And you shall eat before the Lord your God
phrases.notes: דברים 14:23

phrases.english: the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil",
inside, yes; outside, no.
phrases.notes: Inside means ירושלים. Since the פסוק allows eating only there, it follows that eating outside is not allowed.

phrases.english: Why do I need the Merciful One to write:
"You may not eat within your gates
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17

phrases.english: the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your oil"?
To split them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains in detail the claim of step 34 that the פסוקים are extra.
steps.raayaObject: That the פסוק 'you may not eat within your gates' is extra and so comes to split the prohibition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 14:23 already teaches that eating is allowed only inside ירושלים.

steps.title: The second verse is needed for a real prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the first פסוק alone would only teach a rule coming from a positive commandment, not a real לאו. So the second פסוק is not extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that (first) verse, I would have said this is only a positive commandment, but not a real prohibition. Because of this…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof of step 35. It argues that the second פסוק is needed, so it is not extra. The text breaks off at 'because of this', which opens the explanation of what the second פסוק adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'inside yes, outside no' comes from a positive commandment ('you shall eat'). A ban learned that way counts as a עשה and gives no lashes. So the Torah needs the second פסוק, 'you may not eat', to make it a real לאו. That means the second פסוק cannot be the extra one that splits the prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (an early assumption that will be corrected).
This applies only to…
A positive commandment. A ban that is only learned from a עשה gives no lashes.
Because of this, for this reason.

steps.confusionAlert: The first פסוק does forbid eating outside ירושלים. But that ban only has the weight of a עשה, with no lashes. The second פסוק is what makes it a real לאו.

phrases.english: If from that one,
phrases.notes: He means if we had only the first פסוק, 'and you shall eat before ה׳'.

phrases.english: I would have said:
this applies only as a positive commandment,
but as a prohibition, say it does not.
Because of this

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 35 that the second פסוק is extra.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that 'you may not eat within your gates' is extra and free to teach לחלק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first פסוק only gives a ban that comes from a עשה. The second פסוק is needed to make it a real לאו, so it is not extra.
